diagnosis: MRI from a patient with multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1–related pituitary neuroendocrine tumour (PitNET) / pituitary adenoma, presenting with a macrotumour
legend: Coronal MRI reveals a large sellar mass with extensive suprasellar growth measuring approximately 40 mm. The lesion extends laterally into the left cavernous sinus surrounding most of the left internal carotid artery. The lesion extends through the floor of the sella into the sphenoidal sinus. The optic chiasm is draped over the superior aspect of the mass.

diagnosis: 68Ga-DOTA PET-CT in a patient with multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1
legend: This image shows the diagnostic utility of 68Ga-DOTA PET-CT in a patient with multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 with multiple small (< 10 mm) pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours (PanNETs) and metastatic spread to the liver. The functional imaging studies using 68Ga-DOTA PET-CT showed two hotspots corresponding to small PanNETs in the pancreatic head, another hotspot in the ventral pars ascendens of the duodenum (lymph node metastasis), and one larger and one small hotspot in the liver (metastases segment 6 and segments 3/4).

diagnosis: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1–related thymic neuroendocrine tumour (TNET)
legend: A well-differentiated TNET in a patient with multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1. There is global loss of nuclear menin expression in the tumour, supporting multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1–related pathogenesis. Note that the non-tumorous elements at the top of the image show a normal staining pattern for menin.

Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1–related parathyroid disease is characterized by multiglandular multiple adenomas. This photomicrograph shows one of the affected glands with multiple microscopic nodules/adenomas.
Global loss of nuclear menin expression (green bars) is illustrated in multiple pancreatic neuroendocrine microtumours, consistent with multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 syndrome.

diagnosis: Glucagon expression in multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1–related pancreatic neuroendocrine (micro)tumours
legend: Plurihormonality is a common finding in multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1–related pancreatic neuroendocrine (micro)tumours. Glucagon is the most commonly expressed pancreatic hormone, as illustrated in this photomicrograph.
